q: For an ergodic measure-preserving system (X,μ,T) and partition 𝒫, the entropy h_μ(T,𝒫) = lim_{n→∞} (1/n) H(𝒫 ∨ T⁻¹𝒫 ∨ … ∨ T^{-(n-1)}𝒫). The Kolmogorov-Sinai theorem states:
opts: h_μ(T) = h_μ(T,𝒫) for every partition 𝒫
h_μ(T) = sup_𝒫 h_μ(T,𝒫) = h_μ(T,𝒫) for any generating partition 𝒫
h_μ(T) = h_μ(T,𝒫) + h_μ(T,𝒬) for any two partitions
h_μ(T) = H(𝒫) for the finest partition
exp: Kolmogorov-Sinai theorem: h_μ(T) = h_μ(T,𝒫) for any generating partition 𝒫 (one where ∨_{n=-∞}^∞ T^n𝒫 separates points). This is the key computational result: entropy can be computed from a single generating partition rather than taking the supremum.
